summary: Frontend hot-zones inspected: cookie attributes, JWT-out-of-JS, withAuth 6-step, Idempotency-Key generation/forwarding, CSP, dangerouslySetInnerHTML ban, server/client-component boundary, INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET absence. Cookie attribute discipline is mostly correct (HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax+Secure-on-prod on every Set-Cookie that issues a token). JWT never read by JS. crypto.randomUUID() is the sole idempotency key generator. INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET is absent from the frontend bundle and runtime. CSP omits unsafe-eval. dangerouslySetInnerHTML is absent and ESLint-blocked. However: (1) the dedicated /api/checkout/commit and /api/payment/simulate route handlers required by the TD do NOT exist; both endpoints fall through to the generic [...path] catch-all which never forwards the Idempotency-Key header to the backend, breaking checkout replay-safety (CHK-009) and the payment idempotency contract — every Place-Order tap reaches checkout.commit without the key, defeating server-side dedup. (2) clearAccessCookie/clearRefreshCookie OMIT SameSite and Secure attributes, so production clears emit a Lax-default cookie with no Secure flag — RFC-compliant browsers may still accept the clear, but browsers that only update an existing cookie when the new attributes match (SameSite mismatch on clear is a known footgun) can leave the original session cookie in place. (3) withAuth steps 5/6 are reordered relative to the TD pseudocode: the implementation calls downstream() with the new access token BEFORE rotating cookies on the response. If downstream() returns a stream or sets its own cookies, the Set-Cookie order is fine, but step 5 in the TD says rotate first; verified equivalent in practice but recommend matching the spec ordering to avoid future drift. (4) /orders and /orders/[id] do server-side fetches via http://localhost:3000 (NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL fallback) — environment-leaky and brittle in production. (5) Layout.tsx renders Header (Client) and TabBar (Client) globally — including on /login, /admin, etc. — which forces a fetch('/api/auth/session') on every navigation. Functionally OK but adds unnecessary fan-out. Three findings rated high/medium block the run; remainder are low/style nits.

findings.description: The TD requires DEDICATED handlers at /api/checkout/commit and /api/payment/simulate that read the client's Idempotency-Key (body field per TD or HTTP header per the current client) and forward it as the 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header to the backend. Neither dedicated handler file exists — both endpoints fall through to the generic /api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts catch-all. That catch-all does not read or forward the Idempotency-Key header (line 62-65 only sets Content-Type and Authorization). Result: every checkout commit and payment simulate reaches the backend without an Idempotency-Key, defeating server-side replay-dedup. CheckoutCommitButton (app/checkout/CheckoutCommitButton.tsx:23-30) does send the header to the frontend route handler, but that header is dropped at the proxy boundary. This is a replay-safety violation per CHK-009 and a financial-correctness risk for a re-clicked Place Order on a flaky network. The catch-all itself even acknowledges the gap in its STUB NOTE comment (line 11-15).
findings.recommendation: Either (a) create dedicated route files: app/api/checkout/commit/route.ts and app/api/payment/simulate/route.ts that wrap withAuth, read the incoming 'Idempotency-Key' header (or body field 'idempotencyKey' per TD), and forward it as 'Idempotency-Key' on the downstream POST; or (b) modify the [...path] catch-all to forward an 'Idempotency-Key' header from the incoming request when present (req.headers.get('idempotency-key')) onto the downstream call. Option (a) matches the TD topology and is the documented intent. Add a unit test asserting the header reaches the upstream fetch via fetch-mock interception.
cwe_refs: CWE-837 Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action

findings.description: Cookie-clear strings omit SameSite and Secure attributes that are present on the corresponding build*Cookie functions. Some browser cookie-store policies (e.g., Chromium's strict matching of SameSite/Secure when overwriting) will treat a Set-Cookie that lacks Secure on an HTTPS origin as an attempted downgrade and ignore the overwrite, leaving the original HttpOnly+Secure session cookie alive after AUTH_REVOKED or /api/auth/logout — a session-fixation / failed-logout footgun. Path attribute matches but is not sufficient. This violates the TD security_posture.cookies.clearance contract ('cleared via Set-Cookie name=; Max-Age=0; same Path' is incomplete — same Path is necessary but not sufficient).
cwe_refs: CWE-1004 Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag (analogous SameSite/Secure absence)

findings.description: Server Components manually reconstruct the cookie header and call back through their own /api/proxy/order/* handler over HTTP using `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'`. Three problems: (a) NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is not declared in .env.example and not part of the TD's service_endpoints_env, so production deployments will silently use the localhost fallback and self-loop fail; (b) Server Component → own-API roundtrip is unnecessary in App Router — direct backend call (matching the pattern used in app/page.tsx and app/products/page.tsx) is simpler, faster, and avoids the fragile baseUrl construction; (c) the proxied path '/api/proxy/order/list' is only two segments after 'proxy'; the catch-all maps that to `${BACKEND_ORDER_URL}/api/v1/order/list` — which contradicts the rest of the codebase (cart calls `/api/proxy/cart/cart/read` → 3 segments → `/api/v1/cart/cart/read`). Either the order backend uses a different route convention or the order pages will 404 in integration.
findings.recommendation: Inline the order list/detail fetch in the Server Component against `${process.env.BACKEND_ORDER_URL}/api/v1/order/...` with the access cookie's Bearer token attached (use lib/auth.readCookie + lib/http.callBackend). Drop NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL entirely. Confirm the actual order backend route shape with the order-component TD.
cwe_refs: CWE-1188 Insecure Default Initialization of Resource

findings.description: Two latent bugs in the 6-step orchestrator: (a) On the refresh-then-downstream path, when downstream() throws (line 204-206) the function returns a 502 BUT the new accessToken/refreshToken from a successful refresh are NOT written back as Set-Cookie. The user's old (just-rotated-on-the-server) refresh token is now considered consumed by identity, but the browser still holds the old one — the next request will refresh-fail and force re-login even though the server actually issued new tokens. (b) The TD pseudocode rotates cookies on a NEW Response wrapping `downstreamRes.body, downstreamRes.status, headers`; the implementation does the same (line 214-217), but if downstreamRes carried its own Set-Cookie headers (currently none do, but a future backend that sets cookies would have them merged via `new Headers(downstreamRes.headers)` on line 210), the order of Set-Cookie entries would be: backend cookies, then access, then refresh — generally fine, but worth a unit test guarding it.
findings.recommendation: Refactor the post-refresh path: build a `mutableHeaders` containing both Set-Cookie entries first, then call downstream(); on success, copy downstreamRes.body+status into a Response with the merged headers; on downstream throw/timeout, still return 502 BUT include the rotated Set-Cookie headers so the browser advances to the new tokens (otherwise the next request fails). Add a unit test: 'refresh succeeds, downstream times out → response has both rotated Set-Cookies and a 502 envelope'.
cwe_refs: CWE-672 Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions

findings.description: TD security_posture.csrf states 'All mutating route handlers require Content-Type: application/json (rejects form-urlencoded), blocking naive HTML-form CSRF.' Implementation does not enforce this: (a) the [...path] catch-all silently coerces non-JSON bodies into `{}` (line 53-55) — a same-site or sub-resource form-urlencoded POST is accepted with empty body, potentially triggering side-effecting backend actions like cart/cart/add-item with default server semantics; (b) /profile/page.tsx renders a `<form action='/api/proxy/identity/auth/logout' method='post'>` which sends application/x-www-form-urlencoded by default — the logout handler does not check Content-Type, so this works today, but it directly contradicts the stated CSRF defense and undermines the documented invariant. SameSite=Lax cookies do mitigate cross-site form CSRF, so this is medium not high, but the gap-vs-spec is real.
findings.recommendation: Add a tiny `requireJsonContentType(req)` helper in lib/http.ts that returns a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR when `req.headers.get('content-type')` does not start with 'application/json'. Apply it to every mutating route handler ([...path] catch-all, login, logout, refresh — except where intentionally accepting form posts; in that case change /profile/page.tsx logout button to use a Client fetch() with JSON body, matching Header.tsx).
cwe_refs: CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

findings.description: Public passthrough handler reads the access cookie WITHOUT any expiry check and forwards the raw cookie value as a Bearer token to the catalog backend. If the access token is expired, the backend will reject with AUTH_INVALID and the customer sees an upstream error instead of a clean 'no auth = public' fallback. More importantly: a stale or tampered access cookie could be forwarded as a Bearer header, leaking expired tokens into upstream logs. The TD said 'if access cookie present forward Bearer (no behavior change for catalog list)' — but the spec assumed a present-AND-valid cookie. The implementation matches the literal TD wording; the spec should be tightened or the code should call decodeJwt+isExpired before attaching the Bearer.
findings.recommendation: Reuse decodeJwt + isExpired from lib/auth.ts. Forward the bearer only when present AND not expired. Otherwise omit Authorization entirely. Same fix applies anywhere we forward an access cookie on a public passthrough route.

findings.description: Header is a Client Component rendered on EVERY route by the root layout, including /login, /register, /admin and embedded /api routes' fallback HTML. Every navigation triggers fetch('/api/auth/session'). The TD calls for a SessionContext populated once per top-level navigation and consumed by Client Components — Header re-fetches per-mount. Also: a /login redirect target uses encodeURIComponent(pathname) (good) but pathname can be a deeply-nested encoded path; combined with router.push(nextParam) on /login (line 49), an attacker-supplied next can cause an open-redirect to javascript: or //evil.com if the value isn't a same-origin path. The current Login uses router.push(nextParam) without same-origin validation.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the layout in a server-side SessionContext provider that runs probeSession once and pipes {authenticated, user} via a Client provider. In /login on submit, validate `nextParam` starts with '/' and not '//' (open-redirect) before router.push.
cwe_refs: CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

findings.description: TD security_posture.csp_no_unsafe_eval explicitly says 'unsafe-eval is NOT included' (correct) and acknowledges 'unsafe-inline for script-src is a known Next.js App Router constraint pre-nonce-middleware; tracked as a follow-up to add per-request nonces.' The current next.config.js leaves 'unsafe-inline' in but does NOT carry a code-comment pointing back to the TD note or the follow-up; future maintainers will not know it's a documented exception. Also: connect-src 'self' is included but font-src and img-src deviate from the TD baseline (no font-src; img-src omits 'data:' is OK but the TD baseline includes data: explicitly). Minor.
findings.recommendation: Add a code-level comment at script-src/style-src lines linking to the TD section. Bring font-src into the array (the TD lists fonts.gstatic.com). Re-confirm CSP with the design team before merging.
cwe_refs: CWE-1021 Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers (analogous to incomplete CSP coverage)

findings.description: Login route handler explicitly strips raw tokens from the client response body (good — matches spec), but `rest.user ?? rest` (line 68) falls back to `rest` (which after token-strip would be an empty object, but if the upstream changed shape and put more fields at the top level, those would leak unexpectedly to the client). Defense-in-depth: explicitly destructure the only intended fields (user object) and never spread `rest` to the client.
findings.recommendation: Replace `data: rest.user ?? rest` with `data: rest.user ?? null`. If the upstream omits user, return null and let the client treat it as a successful login without echoing arbitrary upstream fields.

findings.locus: frontend/lib/idempotency.ts:13-15 (and call sites in CheckoutCommitButton + PaymentSimulator)
findings.description: generateIdempotencyKey() exists but neither call site uses it — both inline `crypto.randomUUID()` directly. Functionally identical, but the helper exists so we can drop a Math.random() fallback or polyfill in one place if a target browser ever lacks crypto.randomUUID(). InFlightMap is exported but unused — TD specifies its use in CheckoutCommitButton; the actual button uses a useState `loading` flag (functionally equivalent for single-button single-tab use) but does NOT match the documented architecture. No correctness risk in MVP single-tab usage.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) call generateIdempotencyKey() in the two call sites (matches TD), or (b) delete the helper and InFlightMap to avoid dead code. Pick one and align tests. Advisory; no cycle.
